textbookText: A. Tick the correct alternative. 1. What type of leaves do submerged hydrophytes typically have? a. large, flat and with a waxy coat b. Thin, small and translucent c. Broad, with prominent veins d. Needle like and succulent 2. Name the category to which the given plant belong to?

a. Submerged floating b. Rooted submerged c. Free floating d. Rooted emergent 3. How do xerophytic leaves minimize the rate of transpiration? a. By increasing the size of leaf blades b. By reducing the concentration of waxy coating on leaf surfaces c. By developing shiny and glazed leaf surfaces d. By increasing the density of stomata 4. Which category of xerophytes completes its life cycle in a short period of time when sufficient moisture is available? a. Succulent b. True xerophytes c. Ephemerals d. Drought resistants 5. What is the another term used to describe ephemerals? a. Drought avoiders b. Moisture evaders c. Drought escapers d. Water seekers 6. Which of the following is an example of a plant belonging to the category of ephemerals? a. Aloe b. Acacia nelotica c. Solanum xanthocarpum d. Begonia

B. Answer the following questions: 1. What is ecological adaptation? Why is it important for species survival? 2. How do plants adapt to environments where not all necessary needs are provided? 3. Explain the anatomical and physiological adaptations of hydrophytes to their aquatic environment. 4. How do ephemerals adapt to an dry environment? 5. Explain the concept of xerophytes and their adaptations to arid environments. 6. What distinguishes true xerophytes from other categories in terms of their adaptation to arid conditions? ***** Biology, Grade 11 | 210
